record.name: Georgia
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. In July 2026 the economy minister said the government is working on a national AI strategy and establishing the country's first AI research centre in Kutaisi. A Digital Governance Agency report of 20 October 2026 reports discussion of the process of developing the national AI strategy.

next_check.reason: Adoption of the national AI strategy and the mandate of the Kutaisi AI research centre.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. No retained English query. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Checked the cited article quotation in cached HTML and attempted one rendered-text retrieval; the visible rendering remains unverified. This was a partial source-evidence check, not a full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. Both English searches found AI strategy and research-centre activity, not a government-designated evaluator of advanced models. The retrieved Digital Governance Agency English page describes the Ministry of Justice's role in safe public-sector AI, legal and institutional mechanisms, and the Georgia–Korea Digital Cooperation Center. This is useful primary governance context, but not an exhaustive national institutional inventory or proof that no institute exists. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Georgia national AI safety security institute advanced model evaluation proposal government

check.language_note: The recorded ka query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The PMCG page is dated 2021 and explicitly retained as background rather than current-position evidence. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: The Digital Governance Agency's report of 20 October 2026 describes the development of the national AI strategy and planned AI-based advisory and self-service initiatives at the House of Justice. This is administrative AI governance, not a national institute to evaluate advanced models. It provides bounded primary governance context, not proof of absence or a complete national inventory.

record.notes: The minister's statement was reported by Imedi (secondary) on 18 July 2026, from a meeting on global AI governance in Shanghai; no government release was found. A strategy or research centre would not count without a model-evaluation mandate. The earlier 2021 PMCG study is background only.
